response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30. Note: the prior report text conflicts with the prior images. It says heart size normal, but the heart is enlarged on the prior PA image. It mentions no device, but a left pectoral cardiac device is present on the prior image. Verify that the report belongs to this image.
TECHNIQUE: Current is AP, labeled supine, portable, with low inspiration and mild rotation. Prior is PA, appears upright, with adequate inspiration and mild rotation. Projection, position, inspiration and rotation all differ from the prior. Comparability is limited (both blind reads agree).

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1: Tubular density over the tracheal air column, consistent with an endotracheal tube, tip over the upper thoracic trachea. The carina is not clearly seen, so the tip-to-carina relationship is unconfirmed. Not present on the prior. The indication does not mention intubation. Status is indeterminate: the recorded reads disagreed (read A: new, read B: stable). A merge note says this may be a pairing artifact, with both reads calling the tube new and the cardiac device stable. The resident should verify.
- F3 (right mid zone) and F4 (left mid zone): Increased coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacity, both reads agree. The pattern is consistent with interstitial fluid or another diffuse process. Supine AP technique contributes to part of the appearance.
- F5 (right lower zone) and F6 (left lower zone): Hazy basal opacity, indeterminate, both reads agree. Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.
- Triage: critical tier, on-call page flagged. Reason: new endotracheal tube with tip level unconfirmed, new bilateral hazy lung opacities, supine film limits comparison.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is roughly midline allowing for rotation. A tubular density projects over the trachea, consistent with an endotracheal tube (F1, indeterminate, reads disagreed on status as above), tip over the upper thoracic trachea, carina not clearly seen. Lung volumes are low. Bilateral coarse reticular and hazy opacities are present in the perihilar, mid and lower zones, with denser hazy opacity at the right base and at the left base and retrocardiac region. No focal mass is seen within the limits of the film. Prior had no tube, well inflated lungs, mild right perihilar and lower zone marking prominence, and no confluent consolidation, nodule or mass.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum looks broad on this AP supine film, so width is not reliable (F8, indeterminate, only one read recorded this finding). Hila are indistinct with perihilar haze, more evident on the right. Prior: mediastinal contour not widened for a PA film, hila mildly prominent on the right with rotation contributing, no discrete hilar mass.
- Pleura: No pleural line is seen, but a supine film is insensitive for pneumothorax. Hazy increased density over both lower zones with indistinct costophrenic regions. Layering effusions cannot be excluded. Prior: no pneumothorax, no large effusion, left costophrenic angle partly obscured by the enlarged heart.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both films (F7, indeterminate). Interval change in size cannot be judged because the AP supine low-volume projection magnifies the heart. Left heart border is partly indistinct. A left pectoral cardiac device with multiple transvenous leads is present, including shock coils over the SVC and right ventricle regions, with further lead tips over the cardiac silhouette (F2). Same lead configuration on both films, no lead discontinuity at this resolution. F2 status is indeterminate: the recorded reads disagreed (read A: stable, read B: new), and the merge note suggests a pairing artifact. The right ventricular coil projects lower on the current film, which is expected from the projection, position and inspiration change.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib or clavicle fracture is seen, though fine bone detail is limited on the portable film. No soft tissue gas. No definite focal bone lesion at this resolution. Both domes are high, consistent with low inspiration and supine position. The left dome is poorly defined behind the heart. No free gas is seen, though a supine film is insensitive for this. ECG electrodes and external lines overlie the chest. A looped density over the lower midline may be an enteric tube or external hardware.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Increased hazy and reticular opacity in the right mid zone (F3) and left mid zone (F4), both reads agree. Basal opacities are denser on the right and the left hemidiaphragm is poorly defined (F5, F6), but these are indeterminate because of technique. A tubular density over the trachea is not on the prior (F1, indeterminate, reads disagreed on status). Size change is not applicable for these findings.
- Unchanged: Left pectoral cardiac device with similar lead configuration on both films (F2, indeterminate, reads disagreed on status). Enlarged cardiac silhouette is present on both films, but interval size change is not comparable. No discrete lung mass or nodule is seen on either film within the limits of each film. No displaced fracture is seen on either film.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine portable with low inspiration. Magnification differs between the two. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT chest if clinically needed. (Reads A and B)
- Are pleural effusions present, and are they new? | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and appears as hazy density rather than a meniscus. Both bases are hazy, with low volumes also contributing. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest. (Read A)
- Is there a left pleural effusion or left lower zone collapse behind the heart? | Reason: Retrocardiac density on a single frontal supine film, with an enlarged heart and a poorly defined left hemidiaphragm. | Recommend: Lateral view when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest. (Read A)
- Is the basal opacity true consolidation or atelectasis from low volumes? | Reason: Current film is supine with low lung volumes, which crowds the lower zones and mimics basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration when possible, or CT chest. (Read A, related to F5)
- Is the endotracheal tube tip at a satisfactory level above the carina, and is an enteric tube present? | Reason: The carina is not clearly defined on this compressed image. Multiple external lines and a looped density over the lower midline overlap the mediastinum and upper abdomen. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film after removing external lines from the field if position remains unclear. (Read A, related to F1)
- Have the cardiac device lead tips moved? | Reason: Different projection, position and inspiration change the projected position of the leads over the heart. | Recommend: Review in PACS against the prior. If displacement is a clinical concern, obtain PA and lateral films when the patient is able and a device check. (Read A)
- Is there a small pneumothorax? | Reason: A supine film is insensitive, because air collects anteriorly and at the bases. No pleural line is seen, but that does not exclude it. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if clinically suspected. (Reads A and B)
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider than before? | Reason: AP supine projection and rotation widen the mediastinal shadow compared with the PA upright prior. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if clinically indicated. (Read A, related to F8)
- Are there small lung nodules on either study? | Reason: The portable film has low contrast and diffuse opacities. The device generator and external hardware obscure parts of both lungs. Small nodules are not reliably seen on X-ray. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant. (Read A)
- Are there pleural effusions, and are they new? | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as a hazy veil. The lower zones are also crowded by low volumes. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest. (Read B)
- Is there a left pleural effusion or retrocardiac collapse or consolidation? | Reason: The left base is hidden behind the heart on a low-volume supine AP film. The left costophrenic angle was already slightly hazy on the prior. | Recommend: Upright PA and lateral when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest. (Read B)
- Is the basal opacity true new airspace disease or an effect of technique? | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest. (Read B, related to F5)
- Is an endotracheal tube present, and where is its tip relative to the carina? Is an enteric tube present, and where does it end? | Reason: The tube outline and carina are not clearly resolved on this compressed image, and overlying leads and wires confuse the midline. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing and confirm tube positions clinically. Repeat the film if the tip is not seen. (Read B, related to F1)
- Is the mediastinum widened? | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation and low volumes widens the mediastinal shadow. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern. (Read B, related to F8)

IMPRESSION:
1. Tubular density over the trachea, consistent with an endotracheal tube, not present on the prior. Tip projects over the upper thoracic trachea and the carina is not clearly seen, so the tip-to-carina relationship is undetermined. Indeterminate, and the recorded reads disagreed on status. The indication does not mention intubation. Confirm promptly.
2. Increased bilateral coarse reticular and hazy perihilar and mid zone opacities (right mid zone and left mid zone, both reads agree), consistent with interstitial fluid or another diffuse process. Infection or another diffuse process is not excluded on a supine, low-volume film. Supine AP technique contributes to part of the appearance.
3. Hazy right lower zone opacity, indeterminate (both reads agree). Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.
4. Hazy left base and retrocardiac opacity with a poorly defined left hemidiaphragm, indeterminate (both reads agree). Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.
5. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both films. Interval change cannot be judged. Left pectoral cardiac device with the same lead configuration on both films, status indeterminate with the recorded reads disagreeing.
6. Pleural effusion, pneumothorax, true mediastinal widening and small nodules remain undetermined. No discrete lung mass or definite focal bone lesion is seen at this resolution.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source image in PACS with windowing now to confirm endotracheal tube position relative to the carina and to check for an enteric tube. Repeat chest radiograph if the tip is not seen, after removing external lines from the field.
- Upright PA and lateral chest radiograph when the patient is able, to reassess heart size, mediastinal width and basal opacities.
- Upright or decubitus chest film, or bedside ultrasound, for pleural effusion and small pneumothorax if clinically suspected.
- CT chest if clinically indicated, for undetermined basal opacity, effusion, mediastinal width or small nodules.
- Cardiac device check if lead displacement is a clinical concern.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
